- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon.
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then decline too sharply, suggesting overshoot after spikes.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized; true outcomes often pull back from forecast highs, especially after 10–15 days.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to recent price drops; true outcomes often dip before model forecasts adjust.
- Forecasts are overly sensitive to recent volatility; smoothing recent spikes reduces overprediction.
- Model underreacts to low-price periods; true outcomes show stronger downward momentum when model is flat or rising.
- Horizon-specific: Day 1–3 forecasts are often too high; later days (10–30) show more accurate alignment but still biased upward.
- Adjust forecasts downward by 2–5% for the first 5 days, then apply a decay factor (e.g., 0.95 per day) to reduce overconfidence in later days.
